prompt:
Create exactly one new hero-character master illustration of Vivhite for a fantasy deckbuilding game's animated character-selection scene, using only the three supplied references. Image 1 controls her exact body proportions, costume construction, color palette and overall identity; do not reproduce any outer glow visible there. Image 2 controls the authoritative magical-girl outfit construction, asymmetric shoulders, butterfly ornament and accessories. Image 3 controls refined facial features, silver hair texture, purple eyes and delicate gold spectacles.

Draw the same Vivhite as an elegant magical-girl hero and pure unarmed spellcaster. Preserve her short layered silver-white bob, vivid violet-pink eyes, thin round gold glasses, cyan-to-cobalt butterfly, black and navy gold-trimmed hair ornaments, dark high collar, faceted violet pendant, asymmetric black-white-navy shoulder construction, white and pale-lavender dress panels, fine gold trim, segmented white forearm guards and pleated magical-girl skirt.

Use one single vertical three-quarter-length hero composition, showing everything from the top of the complete butterfly ornament and hair through the skirt and upper thighs. Present her in a near-front three-quarter hero pose: torso turned 20 to 35 degrees toward screen-left, face and calm gaze also directed toward screen-left and the center of the future selection screen, upright elegant posture, subtle contrapposto and a self-possessed, cool, faintly cute expression. The silhouette must carry visual motion toward screen-left rather than toward screen-right. This is a character-selection presentation pose, not a combat side profile.

Extend her nearer screen-left empty arm outward toward screen-left at chest height with a softly bent elbow and an open graceful spellcasting palm. Let her farther screen-right empty arm bend gently downward and outward with its relaxed open hand still visible. Keep both arms clearly separated from the torso and skirt, with visible gaps around the shoulders, elbows, wrists and hands. Avoid strong foreshortening. Neither hand may cross the face, glasses, butterfly, pendant, chest or the other arm. Show exactly five natural fingers on each hand.

Design the silhouette for a new custom Spine skeleton and weighted mesh: clean separable head and hair masses, readable shoulder attachment zones, distinct upper arms, forearms and hands, unobstructed torso edges, clear skirt panels and minimal hair overlap across the shoulders. Keep the entire butterfly, hair, elbows, fingertips, skirt hem and upper-thigh cutoff safely inside the image with generous unused margin. Use polished hand-painted 2D anime game key art, elegant clean linework, restrained cel shading, crisp eyeglass rims, coherent lighting confined to the character, solid near-opaque skin and costume interiors and strong shape readability. Every painted mark must end at the physical character contours.

No weapon of any kind: no sword, blade, staff, wand, rod, spear, spellbook, shield, held orb or weapon-like accessory. Nothing held in either hand. No attack stance, side-on fighting pose, crouch, lunge, weapon grip, crossed arms or hands covering the face. No painted material outside the character silhouette. No aura, outer glow, bloom, light fog, haze, mist, smoke, particles, magic circle, spell arc, floating crystal, floor, cast shadow, scenery, environment, decorative frame, typography, logo, signature or watermark. No character sheet, turnaround, sprite sheet, panel grid, inset image, duplicate pose, alternate costume or multiple views. No extra person, extra limb, duplicated hand, duplicated finger, missing finger, cropped butterfly, cropped hair, long ribbon, white silk strip, bandage, helmet or heavy armor.
